page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.4xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 3.9 GHz. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, well aligned with standard enterprise application requirements.

A key hardware attribute of the m8idn family is its integrated local storage configuration. The instance includes a dedicated 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, delivering low-latency, high-throughput local scratch space alongside EBS optimization. Network connectivity is delivered at a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps, supporting high-throughput inter-node communication and data ingestion. There are no discrete GPUs provisioned on this instance type.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of direct-attached NVMe storage and 25 Gbps network bandwidth provides strong resource density for disk-intensive and networking-heavy tasks without requiring separate external high-performance block volumes. However, as instance store volumes are ephemeral, workloads requiring long-term data durability must incorporate automated replication or periodic synchronization to persistent storage services.

The m8idn.4xlarge is suited for transactional databases, in-memory caching systems with local persistence, distributed data processing nodes, continuous integration and build pipelines, and latency-sensitive web application backends requiring fast local scratch storage and robust network capacity.
